title: CLAY COUNTY PROPERTY TAXES
full_story:
The first installment of the 2025 taxes payable in 2026 is due Friday, October 16th.  The second installment is due on Friday, November 20th.

Payment can be made to the Clay County Treasurer using any of the following options, by mail, send your check with the payment stub to the Clay County Treasurer PO Box 88 Louisville, IL 62858.  Mailed payments must be postmarked on or before the due date to avoid penalty.  You can pay at the treasurer’s office in the Clay County Courthouse where they accept cash, checks, cashier’s checks, or money orders.  Please bring your entire bill if you want it stamped to show proof of payment.  Office hours are 8:00 am – 4:00 pm Monday through Friday.  Online payments can be made by credit/debit card by going to govpaynow.com PLC #a00082, there will be a convenience fee charged for online Credit Card payments.  Payment can also be made by placing your payment in the envelope depository at the north entrance of the Clay County Courthouse.  Please include payment stub.

For questions call Clay County Treasurer Stacey Allen’s office at 618-665-3727.

title: SHADOWS OF ELMWOOD
full_story:
Flora Rotary will be hosting its 12th annual Shadows of Elmwood Cemetery Tour tonight and tomorrow night.  Tickets will be available at the Flora Depot.

Ticket sales will start just before 5 pm each evening, with the first wagon leaving at 5 each night.  Tickets are sold until 9 pm and the wagons will go until the last patron has gone through.  Tickets are $8 each unless you purchase a Benefactor Ticket at $25 and go to the front of the line to get on the next available wagon.

The club will also have ride assist tickets for those unable to ride on the hay wagons.  If you are physically unable to ride the wagon, they will have spots available on golf carts that will follow the wagons through the cemetery.  Tickets are reserved for those who are in need, and available on a first come first served basis.

While you wait at the Depot there will be 2 additional skits to keep you entertained and there will be concessions available from Krazy Sweet Treats and Kernel Pops.

All proceeds from the cemetery tour go to Flora Rotary for their projects in the community.  The Rotary Club is currently working on updating Flora Rotary Park and adding improvements at Flora’s Pickleball Courts.

title: VAUGHAN ARRESTED
full_story:
On Tuesday at approximately 11:41pm, Wayne County Sheriff’s Deputies conducted a search of a residence in Rural Fairfield and found 54-year-old Jamie L. Vaughan.

Vaughan was supposed to report to the Wayne County Jail for a sentence earlier in the day but failed to comply.  Deputies took Vaughan in to custody and after a short investigation conducted a search of his residence where they located approximately 14 grams of methamphetamine separated in multiple plastic bags.

Vaughan is being held in the Wayne County Jail, on the previous sentence and additional charges of Escape, Unlawful Delivery/ Possession, with intent to deliver methamphetamine, Unlawful Possession of Drug Paraphernalia, and Violation of conditions of Pre-Trial Release.

All persons are merely accused of the charges against them and are presumed innocent unless proven guilty in a court of law.

title: GEFF FRONTIER DAYS
full_story:
Geff Frontier Days will be held tomorrow with more than 60 vendors expected to set up in the village park.  Organizer Julie Hall said there is an extraordinary vendor turnout offering crafts, food, antiques, farm products, homemade goods and other merchandise.

The Day begins with the Geff Ruritan breakfast at 7 am.  For children, Frog races begin at 9 am, followed by turtle races at 9:30 am.  A most-decorated baby contest and diaper derby will begin at 10 am, with a basketball shoot-out, sack and three-legged races, sawdust pile money hunt and pedal pull following throughout the day.

There will not be a Frontier Days parade this year, but the day’s schedule is packed with traditional events for children and adults to enjoy.  Frontier Days’ traditional ham and beans with cornbread will also be served beginning at 11:30 am in the Ruritan building, with the meal cooked over an open fire.  The quilt show will run from 8:30 am to 4 pm, with a quilting demonstration at the Town Hall at 10 am Car and tractor show registration begins at 9 am, and bingo starts at 2 pm.

Local entertainment is also planned throughout the day.  The Little Miss Geff Frontier Days Pageant for girls ages 6 to 9, will begin at 6 pm closing out the day.

title: NORTH WAYNE PRESCHOOL SCREENINGS
full_story:
The North Wayne Schools are conducting Child Find/Preschool Screenings for children who are 3 to 5-years in age, not yet enrolled in public schools and who will not be Kindergarten eligible in the fall.  Child/Find screening checks each child’s progress in hearing, vision, speech, and other developmental areas.  This screening program is free, and parents will receive immediate feedback on how their child is developing.

The Child Find/Preschool Screening will be held at Johnsonville School on Monday, September 21st.  Appointments are necessary for this free service.

Child Find/Preschool Screening enables you to gain valuable knowledge concerning your child’s development.  The screening procedure takes about 45 minutes, and appointments must be made so that children don’t have a long wait period.  Parents should call 618-673-3044 to make an appointment or to get more information.

The service is a free check of your child’s progress in the development areas, but appointments are needed.  If you live in the North Wayne School District call 618-673-3044 today to make an appointment for your preschooler.

The following items are required for the screening, proof of income, W2 or 2 consecutive pay stubs, and a certified copy of your child’s birth certificate from the courthouse.

title: DRIVE THRU FLU SHOT CLINIC
full_story:
The Clay County Health Department has released their schedule for drive thru Flu shot clinics.  The First will be on Wednesday, September 16th from 9 am to 4 pm at the Health Department.  People wanting flu shots should follow the signs on Wednesday to the carport, no appointment is needed.  Please bring your Medicare Part B Card, HMO Card, Medicaid Card, or insurance card.  If uninsured, underinsured, or insurance is out of network, you may be charged a small administration fee.

There will also be drive through clinics on September 23rd, September 30th, October 7th, October 14th, October 21st and October 28th at the Health Department, from 9 to 4.

The Health Department will also be administering flu shots at the Xenia Community Center on October 7th from 11:30 to 12:30, at the Ingraham Bank on October 8th from 9 to 10 am, at the Louisville Farm Bureau October 13th from 10:15 to 11:15, at the Clay City Bank on October 16th from 9 to 10 am.

The Health Department says getting the flu vaccine is the best way to protect yourself, your family, and your community from the flu.  The Health Department will be administering the trivalent flu vaccine or the higher dose influenza vaccinations.  Different flu strains circulate every flu season, making it important that you get an annual flu shot.

title: IECC TRUSTEE ELECTION
full_story:
Nomination papers for three Trustee seats for the 2027 Consolidated Election are now available in the IECC District Office, 233 East Chestnut Street, in Olney.

Candidates may file nomination petitions during regular business hours from November 16th, at 8:00 am through November 23rd, at 4:30 pm at the District Office.

Should a simultaneous lottery be necessary, the lotteries will be scheduled for Tuesday, November 24th, at 8:30 am.

The election to be held in 2027 will be for three Trustee positions.  The Consolidated Election will be held on April 6th.

A Candidate’s Guide is available for inspection at the State Board of Elections’ website at: https://www.elections.il.gov/Main/Publications.aspx Select “2027 Candidate’s Guide’ under Election Guidelines.

title: CHILD SAFETY SEAT INSPECTIONS
full_story:
On Friday, September 25th the Clay County Health Department will be offering Car Seat Safety checks from Noon until 4 pm.

During this time certified child passenger safety technicians will provide a free car seat safety check.  Is your car seat expired, installed correctly or is it the right seat for your child.  Find out for free and get any questions answered.

Illinois recognizes Child Passenger Safety Week September 20th through 26th, to remind parents and caregivers that state law requires children to ride in a child safety seat until age 8 and rear-facing until age 2.  During this time certified child passenger safety technicians provide free car seat safety checks throughout the state as part of Child Passenger Safety Week.

According to statistics 3 out of 4 Child Safety Seats are installed incorrectly.

title: LAKE LAND NO 1
full_story:
Lake Land College was recently named the number one community college in the nation in education outcomes, as reported in the 2026 Best & Worst Community Colleges study by the personal finance company WalletHub.

The study evaluated 613 community colleges across the nation, with education outcomes used as one of three key dimensions to measure institutional merit.  By receiving the top ranking in the study for education outcomes, Lake Land College was recognized as the number one community college in the nation across several student success metrics, including first year retention rate, graduation rate, transfer rate and student-faculty ratio.

The WalletHub study also named Lake Land College the number one community college in Illinois, ranking it first among 30 statewide colleges.  Along with the education outcomes criteria, this measurement analyzed two additional dimensions; cost & financing and career outcomes; using 18 key performance indicators to measure overall value, quality and long-term student success.  In addition to the highest rating in Illinois, the same measurement ranked Lake Land College as the 62nd best college in the study, placing it among the top 10% of community colleges nationwide.  Lake Land College President Josh Bullock noted that the strong performance throughout the study reflects Lake Land’s ongoing commitment to high-quality, affordable and accessible education.

“These findings reflect our dedication to provide educational pathways that fit and transform our students’ lives,” Bullock said.  “We are pleased to see these efforts affirmed in this study, which only inspires us to continue to serve our students and communities with excellence.  Congratulations to our board, faculty and staff for their leadership and devotion in making Lake Land College one of the nation’s best community colleges.”

The WalletHub rankings represent the latest of Lake Land College’s many national honors.  Lake Land has consistently been named one of the nation’s top community colleges by the Aspen Institute College Excellence Program, with seven consecutive recognitions since 2013.

The full WalletHub study is available on the company’s website at WalletHub.com/edu/e/Best-Worst-Community-Colleges/15076.

Lake Land College offers a wide range of high-demand degrees and certificates in trade, tech and transfer-ready programs.  To learn more or get started, visit the Lake Land College website at LakeLandCollege.edu.
